text: The Fed just raised rates to 3.75%-4% with more hikes possible, GDP growth is slowing to 1.5%, and inflation is stuck at 3.4% — this stagflationary mix means you should be cautious about adding new risk and tighten stops on your weaker holdings.
Trim QBTS because a 41% loss combined with no earnings, 22% short interest, and insider selling is a toxic combination — reduce your exposure and redeploy that capital into stronger positions.

Trim NCLP.L since it's your worst-performing ETF at a 20.7% loss and a large position — in a rising-rate environment with slowing growth, reducing this outsized drag protects the rest of your portfolio.
Raise your BMNR stop from $19.03 to $20.19 to lock in more of your gains while still giving this high-growth name room to run.
Add to Micron — it has the strongest momentum in your portfolio with a bullish MACD and price above its 50-day average, and memory chips remain in a structural upcycle driven by AI demand.
Add to UnitedHealth on this 11% pullback because it's one of the most defensible businesses in healthcare, which is exactly the kind of quality you want to own when the economy is slowing.
Add to Visa while it's only 5% below your cost — its toll-booth business model on global payments generates consistent growth regardless of rate cycles, making it a strong hold through uncertainty.
